questions.question: What is the main difference between analytical and reflective writing?
options: Analytical writing examines something external; reflective writing looks inward at your own experiences
Reflective writing never uses first person
questions.explanation: Analytical writing breaks down texts or events objectively; reflective writing examines your own experiences and learning.

questions.question: Which framework is recommended for reflective writing?
questions.explanation: The Gibbs Cycle structures reflection, moving from description through analysis to an action plan.

questions.question: Which verbs are typical of analytical writing?
questions.explanation: Analytical writing uses verbs like analyze, suggest, reveal and demonstrate to interpret evidence.

questions.question: Is first person acceptable in reflective writing?
options: Yes — reflective writing is personal and honest, written in first person
No, first person is always banned
Only if the teacher approves it
questions.explanation: Reflective writing is by nature personal and uses first person, unlike most analytical writing.

questions.question: What distinguishes analysis from summary?
options: Analysis interprets how and why something works; summary only retells what it says
Summary requires evidence; analysis does not
questions.explanation: Going beyond summary to interpretation is the core of analytical writing.
